children.note: Cooking with devotion and offering first produces no reaction. — "that's clearly a karma Yeah. No reaction. It's offered to Krishna and then it's fed…"

children.topic: Attain perfection by worshipping through work
children.note: Chapter 18 text 46: do the karma the Vedas give you, not sin, and it becomes worship that takes you out. — "by worship of the Lord who is the source of all beings and who is…"

children.topic: Running away is not the answer
children.note: Arjuna wanted to give up fighting and beg; Krishna insists on doing one's work and worshipping Him through it. — "I want to go to the Himalayas and beg. Lord Krishna said no you can't…"

children.topic: Three Rs turn work into worship
children.note: The acharyas' formula: righteous work, reward offered to Krishna, and remembrance of Krishna while working. — "this formula is called three R three R. So if we do these three Rs…"

Righteous is not just honest; it must actually help others rather than damage society, so inflating a government tender fails the test. — "So righteous work means work that helps others, not help myself or not help my…"

Supporting 3,000 families sounds righteous until you learn the product is liquor; the harm to society decides the answer. — "That factory is a liquor factory. So, [laughter] so now is it righteous work or…"

children.topic: Reward: offer the fruit to Krishna
children.note: The second R: whatever the work earns is given to Krishna, partly or wholly. — "We worked but the reward is yours my lord. Either in part or in full.…"
The third R: remember who the work is for. Usually one of the Rs is missing, most often remembrance. — "Lord Krishna tells Arjuna you fight on the battlefield but remember me."

children.topic: Why bad things happen to good people
children.note: Suffering in this body comes from what was done in previous bodies, and the Supersoul saw all of it. — "So this answers the question why do bad things happen to good people. I am…"
We think a wrong nobody saw does not count, but Krishna says: I saw, and I permitted it because you wanted it. — "There were too few rasgulas here in the temple hall. Nobody was there. I ate…"

children.topic: Sun, moon, demigods and Chitragupta also see
children.note: Answer to a question about Chitragupta: even if one hides from all the elements and demigods, the Lord in the heart is always there. — "The sun sees, the moon sees, other demigods see like the air etc. And then…"

children.topic: Why the speaker is called Sri Bhagavan
children.note: Dhritarashtra, Arjuna and Sanjaya are named as speakers, but Krishna's words are marked 'Sri Bhagavan uvaca'. — "There were four speakers in Gita. There's one more speaker. Apart from Arjuna darashtra and…"
Bhagavan means the one who has all strength, knowledge, beauty, fame, renunciation and wealth in full. — "One who possesses all opulences which are usually classified into six. Uh one who has…"

children.topic: Krishna chooses his birth; we do not
children.note: The verse on Krishna's appearance is read from the screen. Unlike us, the Lord is not forced to take birth; he appears by his own will. — "I chose the day. I chose the place. I chose the parents. I even chose…"

children.topic: We chose no parents, place, day, time
children.note: Nobody in the audience chose where or to whom they were born; we come because we are forced to. — "No time, no day, no place, no parents. But Lord Krishna, he's saying I am…"

children.topic: Ishvara: the Lord controls his own coming
children.note: This introduces the third of the five topics, the controller. We call ourselves controllers but control nothing about our birth. — "Now we're looking at the topic of ishwara controller. Lord controls his time to come."
To protect his devotees, to destroy those who disturb them, and to establish the principles of religion. — "Number one to deliver the pious. Number two to annihilate the miscreants. So one is…"
We want to be in the first category, protected as devotees, not in the second. — "We should not disturb Krishna's devotees because if we disturb Krishna's devotees, then he comes…"

children.topic: Absolute Truth is God plus His energies
children.note: Devotees say Absolute Truth rather than God because Krishna is described together with His energies. — "And the absolute truth is God plus. There is a plus. And so this is…"
The ordinary meaning of God; the Absolute Truth adds His energies to this. — "God means generator, operator, destroyer. G O D, right? God, generator, operator, destroyer."

children.topic: Sun with its heat and light
children.note: A sun without heat or light is no sun; the Lord is the energetic and His energies are inseparable from Him. — "So, sun plus its energies. Sun with the heat and light. Similarly, the lord has…"

Krishna describes an inferior material energy and a superior energy, the living entities, who come from Him. — "Material energy means it is made of matter or elements. Earth, water, air, fire, ether.…"

Since spirit and matter are both His energy and nothing exists outside them, Krishna is the source of everything. — "So therefore Lord Krishna is saying everything is my energy. And further on he says…"
Other scriptures lack the emphatic declaration Krishna makes about Himself in the Gita. — "I am who I am. Right? But in the Gita he's saying clearly [snorts] there…"
Chapter 10, Vibhuti-yoga, teaches how to remember Krishna by seeing Him in the things around us. — "how we can see Krishna in everything is chapter 10 Lord Krishna he tells Arjuna…"

Four verses of chapter 10 are widely accepted as the essence of the whole Gita, repeating what Krishna has been saying in earlier chapters. — "Lord Krishna gives us the entire Bhagat Gita in four shlokas. This is known as…"

children.topic: I am the source of everything
children.note: We are souls who came from Krishna; everything we have came from Krishna; so our relationship is to engage in His service. — "I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from me. The…"

children.topic: A finger is useless off the hand
children.note: The finger stands for the soul and the body for Krishna: attached and obedient, the finger is complete and happy; detached, it is thrown away. — "If I want to pick up something with my finger, the finger has to obey…"

children.topic: Pure devotees' thoughts dwell in me
children.note: Text 9: devotees do not serve begrudgingly; they get bliss from serving and from talking about Krishna with one another. — "The thoughts of my pure devotees dwell in me. Their lives are fully devoted to…"
For a devotee, life without Krishna is no life at all, just as a fish must be in water to be happy. — "for devotees living without Krishna is like a fish living without water. Fish cannot live…"

Arjuna asks Krishna to prove He is the Supreme Lord, so Krishna shows the universal form. Chapter 10 was Krishna in everything; chapter 11 is everything in Krishna. — "Krishna is telling Arjuna how he can remember him by seeing everything within this world.…"

children.topic: Time I am, destroyer of the worlds
children.note: Krishna declares Himself as time, come to destroy everyone on the battlefield except the Pandavas. — "worlds and I have come here to destroy all people with the exception of you…"

children.topic: Thousands of heads, arms and legs
children.note: In the universal form Arjuna saw all planets and demigods, and even himself, within Krishna. — "Hundreds and thousands of heads, hundreds and thousands of arms, hundreds and thousands of legs.…"
Arjuna saw the Kaurava and Pandava soldiers being devoured, became frightened, and asked who this form was. — "they were all rushing into the mouth of this form and they were being chewed.…"

children.topic: Krishna is the source of all forms
children.note: Universal form, form of time, four-handed Vishnu form and finally the original two-armed form: chapter 11 settles that Vishnu comes from Krishna, not the reverse. — "So he is the source of all forms. The forehanded, the universal, the kala rupa,…"

children.topic: The Lord is the second knower of all bodies
children.note: Besides the soul, who knows one body partially, there is a second knower, the Supreme Lord, who knows every body completely. — "there is a second knower and that is the Lord. He knows all bodies. He…"

The individual farmer knows only his own land; the lands department knows every parcel in the country. So the Lord knows all bodies while we know only ours. — "But the government official one who's working in the lands department he knows all farms…"

children.topic: Supersoul is the overseer and permitter
children.note: Krishna defines Himself in the body as the proprietor with two functions: to oversee and to permit. — "yet in this body there's another a transcendental enjoyer who is the lord the supreme…"

Out of love the Lord accompanies the soul into every body, watching everything it does and sanctioning what it wants. — "To oversee and to permit. Right? You see there are two words there overseer and…"

children.topic: Seated in the heart: remembrance and forgetfulness
children.note: Krishna in the heart supplies whichever we ask for: if we wish to forget Him He helps us forget, if we wish to remember Him He helps us remember. — "I'm seated in everyone's heart and from me comes remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness. By all…"
The Supersoul is constantly on call; we only need to dial. — "It's like having your own personal doctor, you know, on call. Anything just call and…"

children.topic: Hare Krishna is His speed dial number
children.note: Chant Hare Krishna and He is there before the mantra is even finished. — "This is his speed dial number. Just in case anyone wants to have, you know,…"

children.topic: He picks up, but we stop responding
children.note: Answer to whether Krishna also calls us: He is not limited and answers whoever calls His name; the problem is that we then do not talk to Him. — "We immediately call him, he picks up immediately and then we like oh no, now…"

children.topic: Madhva's two fingers: soul and Supersoul
children.note: Madhvacharya preached vigorously against the earlier school that taught we are God; he held up two fingers to show there are always two knowers, soul and Supersoul. — "We're two separate knowers. We have an acharia. His name was Madva."

children.topic: Two fingers means two separate knowers
children.note: Remember the two fingers: nobody should convince you after today that you are God. — "But Madvachaya used to hold up two fingers like this. Two fingers meaning two"
Supersoul means He can do what the soul cannot: He knows all bodies, not just one. — "just like we have man and then we have superman. Isn't it? So superman does…"

children.topic: Contact with nature conditions the soul
children.note: Because of desires we associate with the three modes of material nature, and this contact changes our original nature. — "Goodness, passion and ignorance. When the internality [cough] comes into contact with nature becomes conditioned…"

Conditioned means altered: as hot air is made cool by an air conditioner, the soul's original nature is changed by the modes. — "coming hot, it goes through an air conditioner and it becomes conditioned to become cool."
The modes tie the soul, and the effect depends on how much one associates with each. — "these are known as the goonas the three goonas and gona literally means rope literally…"

children.topic: Modes are the bars of the prison
children.note: We cannot leave the body at will, nor fly or eat grass in it: bound by the body and the body bound by the world. — "These are like the bars in the prison. See material nature and the world here…"

children.topic: Conditions: shoes off, seat belt, no opening the door
children.note: Entering the temple or boarding a plane carries conditions; this world's condition is that you stay until you develop the desire to return to Krishna. — "you want to come into the temple hall there's one condition what is the condition…"

children.topic: Goodness illuminates, passion binds, ignorance deludes
children.note: Three verses read aloud: goodness conditions by happiness and knowledge, passion by longing and fruitive action, ignorance by madness, indolence and sleep. — "the goodness pure love is illuminating and frees one from all sinful reactions. Those situations…"
Passion binds the soul to fruitive work through endless desire. — "The motor passion is born of unlimited size and longing both son and because of…"

children.topic: Three modes as three primary colours
children.note: Goodness is yellow, passion is red and ignorance is blue. Just as three primary colours mix into every other colour, the three modes mix into every kind of body. — "So if you were to assign these three primary colors to the modes of material…"

children.topic: Red is energetic passion, yellow calm goodness
children.note: Passion is intense activity and endless desires, so it gets red; goodness is calm and composed, so it gets yellow; ignorance gets blue. — "And yellow means calm, composed, uh cool, right? That's goodness."

children.topic: Mixed modes produce millions of bodies
children.note: Every body is a particular combination of the three modes, which is why there are so many species. — "if you combine the three modes you get combinations and according to these combinations you…"

children.topic: Morning goodness, noon passion, night ignorance
children.note: Pair exercise mapping the modes onto the day: fresh and calm in the morning, wide awake and wanting at noon, tired and lazy at night. — "Mode of goodness in the morning. Goodness in the mornings. The mode of passion at…"

children.topic: When the sun is down, inauspicious things happen
children.note: Even for night-shift workers, night generally belongs to ignorance; nobody steals in broad daylight (outside South Africa, he jokes). — "See the sun is down. So when the sun is down all sorts of inospicious…"

children.topic: Modes are always in motion, always fighting
children.note: Not a fixed rule: someone can be sleepy in the morning. One mode takes over the other two, yet a person can be mainly situated in one. — "these modes are always in motion. It is not fixed. Right. They're always in motion.…"

The verses on food read aloud: juicy, wholesome foods are goodness; bitter, spicy, burning foods are passion; stale, decomposed, putrid and untouchable foods are ignorance. — "Foods dear to those in the mode of goodness increase the duration of life, purify…"
Food in ignorance. — "Food prepared more than 3 hours before being eaten. Food that is tasteless, decomposed and…"
Attraction to these foods indicates the mode of ignorance. — "things like mushrooms, untouchable. This is fungi, right? Onion, garlic, all these things are untouchable…"

children.topic: Happiness in the modes: poison and nectar
children.note: Happiness in goodness is poison first and nectar later; in passion nectar first and poison later; in ignorance delusion from beginning to end. — "That's in which the beginning may be just like poison but at the end is…"

children.topic: Student, exams and the World Cup
children.note: In goodness he studies through the torture and passing is nectar; in passion he watches the matches and failing is poison; in ignorance he does not bother at all. — "World Cup is going on. You can't watch the match. You have to study for…"

children.topic: Three gates to hell: lust, anger, greed
children.note: Text 21 of the chapter on divine and demoniac natures: these three are the first-class tickets to hell, so avoid them and the modes that produce them. — "Lust, anger, and greed. Every sane man should give these up for they lead to…"

children.topic: Anger is the younger brother of lust
children.note: When desire is frustrated we become angry; kamanuja means the one born after lust. — "So anger is the younger brother of lust. Another name for anger is kamanuja."

children.topic: One more rasgula: greed the elder brother
children.note: When desire is fulfilled we want more; that is greed, the elder brother who always follows lust. — "Oh, that rasgula was very nice, very tasty. Can I have one more?"

children.topic: Get it: greed. Don't get it: anger
children.note: Lust comes first; both possible outcomes of a desire lead to another of the three gates. — "If we get what we want we become greedy. If we don't get what we…"

children.topic: Modes are invisible bars of a jail
children.note: The modes are also the strings that tie us; reaching goodness leaves only one string to break. — "we say this is like the modes are like the bars of the jail cell.…"

children.topic: Easier to break one rope than three
children.note: Coming to goodness reduces the bondage to one string, which is easier to break. — "it's easier to break one string than to break three, isn't it? If you have…"

children.topic: Go to Krishna, who has no strings
children.note: The easiest way out is to approach the one who is not bound by the modes at all. — "the easiest way is actually to go to a person who has no strings and…"

children.topic: Goodness is the ladder to climb out
children.note: Come at least to goodness; from there management is easier and Krishna consciousness becomes possible, even though goodness itself is eventually left behind. — "It's like a ladder. You use goodness to climb and once you reach the top…"
In ignorance you are sleepy all the time and cannot read the Gita or chant; even eating prasad becomes impossible. — "I have even seen a devotey who was so tired they fell asleep while eating…"

children.topic: Engineer your day to promote goodness
children.note: Divine qualities follow naturally when the day is redesigned around goodness. — "we have to engineer our lifestyle. We have to reinvent our day in such a…"

children.topic: Calm versus hooting in a traffic jam
children.note: Behaviour in a traffic jam shows the difference between a person in goodness and one agitated by passion. — "there people who are calm who are collected they're listening to some lecture or they're…"

One who engages in unfailing devotional service at once transcends the modes; there is no other escape. — "Lord Krishna is saying only through bacti only through devotional service can you transcend the…"

children.topic: Iron rod in fire becomes fire
children.note: By constant association with Krishna, who is above the modes, the devotee takes on Krishna's qualities, as an iron rod in fire becomes red hot and burns like fire. — "You take an iron rod and you put it in fire. Over time, what happens…"

children.topic: Bhakti is the hack, the shortcut out
children.note: Any activity of devotional service, like the temple itself, is not under the modes because it is connected to Krishna. — "bacti is like the hack it's like the means out the shortcut to come out"

A devotee connected to Krishna is not affected by degraded surroundings; likewise devotees chanting on Ratha-yatra did not even notice the market they passed. — "shap praad had to jump over people to enter his room they were lying there…"

children.topic: Desires decide which body we get
children.note: The Lord sees and records every desire and supplies a body suited to fulfil it, in sequence. — "according to our desire and according to the magnitude of our desires Lord Krishna fulfills…"

children.topic: Man who wants to live in water becomes a fish
children.note: Prabhupada's example: someone who spends all day at the Durban beach gets a fish body next life so the desire can be fulfilled naturally. — "why you artificially trying to be a fish next life we'll give you a body…"

children.topic: Meat-eater and tiger, sleeper and bear
children.note: Old Gita editions picture a meat-eater beside a tiger and a heavy sleeper beside a bear: nature gives the body that matches the desire. — "Nature will give a body where you don't have to cook anything. You just go…"
Karma dictates where we take birth and what body we get; like cash, it limits which desires can actually be bought. — "you have cash, you want to buy a house. According to the amount of cash…"

What Arjuna saw was Krishna as time. Whether Arjuna fought or not, the soldiers were already finished; only the Pandavas had return tickets. — "Krishna showed was the kala rupa the form of time. I've already killed all these…"

children.topic: I did the work, you take the credit
children.note: Krishna has already done everything; Arjuna is invited simply to act and receive the credit. — "I have already killed all these people. They're all dead. You cannot help them. But…"

Alexander, the Roman and British empires are all gone, but Arjuna and Hanuman are still spoken of; devotees conquer time. — "Pandovas 5,000 years ago, still going on. That is only 5,000. What about Lord Hanuman?…"

children.topic: This form is not for devotees
children.note: Kala-rupa destroys everyone who is not a devotee; devotees have nothing to fear from it. — "He said except the pandavas this form is not for you. It's not for the…"

children.topic: The cat, the kitten and the rat
children.note: Prabhupada's example: the same mouth of time that means death for the rat carries the kitten to safety. The devotee is the kitten. — "So, kala rupa if we equate it to the cat and then the devotey is…"

children.topic: For the rat it is a one-way ticket
children.note: The soldiers being eaten were the rat in the cat's mouth; the Pandavas were the kittens. — "But the same cat catches a rat, the rat knows now this was a one-way…"

children.topic: Moths into fire, rivers into ocean
children.note: Arjuna saw the envious (Duryodhana, Karna) rushing in like moths into fire, while the favourable (Bhishma, Drona) merged like rivers into the ocean. — "those who are enimical to Krishna but those who are favorable to Krishna he says…"

children.topic: Dhruva stood on the head of death
children.note: Dhruva Maharaja's fearlessness shows how devotees relate to time; yet, like Arjuna, they do not wish to see this form and ask for the two-armed form. — "Duva Maharaj. When death came, he stood on the head of death. He told death…"

children.topic: Remember Krishna at death, go to Krishna
children.note: Chapter 8: one who leaves the body remembering Krishna attains His nature without doubt. — "if you remember Lord Krishna at the time of death you go to Krishna At…"

children.topic: Personal assistant flies with the boss
children.note: A good assistant travels and stays with the boss; a devotee stays with Krishna in His abode. — "If the personal assistant is serving nicely, they say, oh, no, no, you know, two…"

children.topic: Whatever you think at death, you attain
children.note: Two points: a controlled mind lets us think of Krishna at death, and our final thought decides our next state. — "Whatever thoughts you have at the time of death that state you will attain"

children.topic: Can I just remember Krishna at death?
children.note: The lecturer dismantles the idea of enjoying freely now and remembering Krishna only at the end. — "I'll remember Krishna at the time of death up till that point I can do…"

children.topic: No expiry label on our heads
children.note: Death can come anytime, as the Nepal floods showed; even a Baba's astrology date does not help. — "Does anyone know when they're going to expire? Did we come with the expiry label…"
When the cat caught it, the parrot's real attachment came out; whatever we put in is what comes out at death. — "The parrot wasn't saying ram ram ram. [laughter] Yeah. Parrot was saying cow cow cow."

children.topic: Spot exam: ready because you studied daily
children.note: If we always think of Krishna, the time of death does not matter. — "Today is your spot exam, you know." Okay, I'm ready. I studied."
Chanting is already the shortcut; we still have to put in the work and make thinking of Krishna our default. — "in kalyuga everyone is looking for a shortcut cut in the shortcut. So we already…"

The verse read from the screen gives the timing of the Lord's appearance: when irreligion rises and religion declines. — "Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice or descendants of a prominent…"

Krishna tells Arjuna to fight and win glory because the outcome is already decided; Arjuna's role is only to be the instrument. — "So Lord Krishna said, "I've already dealt with everything. I've already sorted everything. You just need to be an instrument."

children.topic: Pandavas argue who was the greatest warrior
children.note: After the war Bhima, Arjuna and the brothers debated who won the battle; Krishna declined to judge and sent them to a witness. — "Bhima was saying I killed 100 sons of the koravas of of the of duryodhan…"

Bhima's son Barbarika, who watched the whole battle as a head without a body, saw only Krishna doing everything. — "he said no I could only see Krishna all over the battlefield fil killing everyone.…"

children.topic: Central message: surrender and be used
children.note: Pure devotees know they are doing nothing; Prabhupada always said his guru had sent everyone to help him. When devotees think 'I am doing', Krishna sends reminders. — "that's why he's saying nima matram become an instrument and this is the again the…"

The relationship is reciprocal and sweet; it cannot be understood without engaging in devotional service oneself. — "the harder the devotees try to serve Krishna the harder Krishna serves the devotees we…"

children.topic: Mind can be friend or enemy
children.note: Krishna's teaching in chapter 6 that the mind is the friend of one who has conquered it and the enemy of one who has not. — "Mind can be the friend and can also be the enemy. Now, how does it…"
The difference is simply who is in charge: you or the mind. — "So if we are able to control the mind then it becomes our friend. If…"

children.topic: No link with the Lord without mind control
children.note: Martial arts, studies or any spiritual path all require a controlled mind. — "We cannot link up with the supreme without mind control. Any path you take, any…"

children.topic: Are you using the phone or is it using you?
children.note: An audience exercise that sets up the mind as a tool that can either serve us or hijack us. — "Are you using the phone or is the phone using you? Okay. Quickly to the…"

children.topic: Phone hijacks time like the mind
children.note: A five-minute break becomes hours down a rabbit hole; the mind does the same thing to us. — "The phone somehow hijacks the time, isn't it? So, you have a schedule."

children.topic: Mind is a tool, like a knife
children.note: A knife or phone is good or bad depending on use; so is the mind. — "the phone is a tool. Just like here Lord Krishna will say the mind is…"

children.topic: Give the mind a ring to stay in
children.note: Boxers stay in the ring; the mind needs a boundary too. That boundary is regulation. — "So that's the frame that the speaker has to be in. Cannot leave. So we…"
The speaker's frame on stage stands for the limits regulation gives to the mind. — "The speaker or the presenter cannot go out of that red circle. Has to be…"
The rope stands for regulation that keeps the mind from running away. — "the bull can move around as much as the rope allows, but not more than…"

children.topic: Arjuna: mind harder to control than wind
children.note: Hearing the full dhyana yoga process, Arjuna protests that the flickering mind is impossible to control, and Krishna agrees it is difficult. — "It may be possible to control the wind but I find to control the mind…"

children.topic: Practice and detachment control the mind
children.note: Krishna's answer to Arjuna: abhyasa (regular practice) and vairagya (detachment). — "abiasa and vayaya these are the two tools that Lord Krishna mentions to control the…"

children.topic: Chanting the maha mantra is our practice
children.note: For devotees, abhyasa means regular chanting of Hare Krishna. — "What practice do we employ to help us control the mind? Chanting of the mahantra.…"

children.topic: Mantra frees the mind by constraining it
children.note: Man means mind, tra means to free; the holy names anchor the mind and give it a place to rest. — "Ironically freeing the mind means constraining it. Right? We are we usually have the opposite…"

children.topic: Rules of detachment in our lifestyle
children.note: Vairagya for devotees means the regulative principles: no tea, coffee, liquor, meat, eggs or fish. — "There are some rules and regulations we give to ourselves in our lifestyle that help…"

children.topic: British lord who wanted to be a brahmana
children.note: People find the principles hard only because they lack the right frame; with it they are not hard at all. — "can make you a brahmana no follow these four rules. And then the Lord said…"
Krishna's method for controlling the mind begins with a regulated lifestyle. — "So one who is regulated in his eating vihara means to sleep. One who is…"

children.topic: Breakfast in traffic, lunch at the desk
children.note: Modern life with no fixed time or diet for eating makes the mind impossible to control. — "they're having breakfast in traffic because they got late. Yeah. Either they have some coffee…"

children.topic: Catching up sleep on the weekend
children.note: Irregular sleep, early, late or none at all, keeps the mind unsteady. — "So I spent the weekend catching up my sleep, right? It doesn't work that way…"
Arjuna asks why people do what they should not; Krishna names lust as the driver. — "Arjuna is saying why do people do v karma? Why do they want to perform…"

children.topic: All-devouring sinful enemy of the world
children.note: Controlled by intelligence and knowledge, lust stops vikarma and karma so only akarma remains. — "See lust is very very it's the all devouring sinful enemy of the world. It…"
Nobody teaches a child to lie; sin comes naturally because lust is already within. — "you just leave a rasgula on the table and the child is roaming around and…"

children.topic: Control senses by knowledge, steady the mind
children.note: The closing point; where that spiritual intelligence comes from is tomorrow's topic (chapters 4-6). — "if you control the senses through knowledge then lust comes under control and that's why…"

children.topic: Mind is the sitting place of lust
children.note: An uncontrolled mind becomes an enemy that pulls us from what we should do, just as lust did in chapter 3. — "the mind is also a sitting place of lust. Lust sits in the mind. So…"

children.topic: Four defects of the conditioned human
children.note: Imperfect senses, the tendency to be illusioned, the tendency to cheat and the tendency to make mistakes - so knowledge from this world cannot be trusted as a final source. — "we as human beings we have some limitations the first one is imperfect senses"

children.topic: We cannot even see our own eyelids
children.note: Stands for imperfect senses: we acquire knowledge through senses that cannot even measure exactly how hot a cup of tea is. — "We have eyes, but we can't see even our own eyelids. So, we're limited by…"
Stands for the tendency to be illusioned: we do not see reality as it is. — "We see a rope lying on the floor from afar. We may think it's a…"
The third defect: presenting guesswork as fact to the whole world. — "we tend to cheat also just like Charles Darwin sat in Galapagos Islands"
The fourth defect; to err is human, so we must trust knowledge from a different source. — "Is there anybody here who has never made a mistake in their life? Now we've…"

children.topic: Knowledge comes down by disciplic succession
children.note: Krishna gave this knowledge to the sun god, and it passed from teacher to disciple; in that chain the knowledge stays guarded and safe. — "the knowledge I'm giving you Arjuna, I had given it to the son god. Son…"
The Sanskrit name for transcendental knowledge: it originates in the spiritual world, not here. — "In Sanskrit it is called dyagyan. Means it is knowledge that is not coming from…"

children.topic: Family recipe passed mother to daughter
children.note: A bunny chow recipe becomes a family recipe by being handed down generation to generation - this is how disciplic succession transmits knowledge. — "Oh, this recipe is a secret recipe of our family and we know how to…"

Everything is learned from someone else; a teacher's authority comes from having received the knowledge from a teacher. — "You cannot have a lecturer teaching at a university and he doesn't have a degree…"

The guru has seen the truth and can explain it, as Prabhupada explains the Gita; otherwise we would rack our brains over it alone. — "just to learn the truth by approaching a special master inquire from and unto him…"

children.topic: What about sins from before we knew?
children.note: An audience question about sins committed before receiving this knowledge, including past lives. — "So what happens previous knowledge and the sinful un unknowingly or knowingly committed sins in…"

children.topic: Knowledge is fire on a mountain of cotton
children.note: The answer: knowledge of who Krishna is burns all sin, even past sins, leaving nothing. — "this knowledge is like fire it burns everything there's nothing remaining right you may have…"
The three things needed to approach a guru; the guru then gives the same knowledge in an easier way. — "one was serve the guru number to inquire submissively. Yes. And submissive. And to be…"
A shopkeeper gives extra to a nice customer and nothing to a rude one; humility draws out the guru's mercy. — "the guru if he sees yes the disciple is humble, it has humility, then he…"

Like doubting whether a university is legitimate, constant doubt in the teacher yields nothing; faith after due diligence is not blind following. — "be some faith. Without faith, then nothing can happen."

Recap of Day 5. Krishna reveals knowledge in ascending levels: soul, then the Lord and His energies, then the most confidential, the loving relationship between the Lord and the soul. — "The very first level of confidential knowledge was that we are the soul not the…"

Devotional service is part of the relationship between Krishna and the soul, which is the top level of the Gita's teaching. — "the most confidential knowledge is the relationship between the lord and the living entity or…"
Chapter 9 adds the third part of knowledge: our relationship with God, the most confidential of all. — "So who is God? Who are we? What is our relation? That is complete knowledge."
Knowing who God is counts as more confidential knowledge than knowing we are the soul. — "The original OG goat is Krishna. Greatest of all time."
The Lord's dealings with His devotees can only be understood by those practising devotional service themselves. — "Why did the pandas have to suffer so much? What is this? Why did Lord…"

children.topic: Boy asking a girl's friends about her
children.note: To love someone you must know about them; Krishna gives us all His details through the Gita and chanting His glories. — "Krishna is doing the same he's telling us where he lives he's telling us his…"

children.topic: Mother tolerates the child pulling her hair
children.note: An outsider misreads the child's behaviour; Krishna's inner circle is entered only through bhakti, the fastest and easiest process. — "mothers tolerate because there's a relation. It's a different relation. And we can't understand that…"

Other editions insert interpretations and do not come in disciplic succession, so they cannot convey what Krishna actually said. — "And we don't read other Gas because other Gas Why don't we read other Gas?…"

children.topic: Hearing the Ramayana and asking who is Sita
children.note: If one finishes the Gita without concluding that Krishna is the Supreme Lord, one has missed the point entirely. — "you heard the whole Ram Ramayan and then at the end of the Ramayan you…"

children.topic: Gita is the milk of the Vedas
children.note: From all the Vedas the one thing to know is Krishna; learning anything else from them is a distraction. — "The milk of the Vedas, the essence of the Vedas. So if we just read…"

children.topic: Best yogi is the bhakti yogi
children.note: Every yoga needs mind control, but the one who abides in Krishna with faith is the highest of all. — "of all the different parts that are there, Lord Krishna is saying the best one…"

children.topic: Offer a leaf, fruit, flower or water
children.note: The famous verse: Krishna, who owns everything, asks only for love, not for the item itself. — "If one offers me with love and devotion a leaf, a fruit, a flower or…"

children.topic: What do you give one who has everything?
children.note: Even pomegranates imported from Iran are nothing next to what Krishna has; He is really asking for love. — "He just told us everything you see is mine. What do you give a person…"

children.topic: Child feeds father from father's plate
children.note: Everything already belongs to Krishna; He accepts our offering because of the love, even a half-bitten biscuit. — "Child is taking whatever is the father's but is giving to the father. So the…"

children.topic: Krishna does not need our love
children.note: We need Krishna; He asks only for simple things anyone anywhere can offer. He is the taste of water. — "Mind you, Krishna does not need our love. It's for our benefit."

children.topic: No bill for sunlight, air or water
children.note: Krishna gives everything free and only asks that we love Him back; then He supplies what devotees lack and protects what they have. — "Anyone in paying a bill for sunlight? You consumed this much sunlight today. Here's your…"

children.topic: Essence: always think of Me, become My devotee
children.note: The hack for life: form a relationship with Krishna, love Him and go back to Him, and true happiness and peace follow. — "This verse Lord Krishna says it twice in the Gita. right here, right in the…"

children.topic: Krishna gives the understanding to reach Him
children.note: Krishna reciprocates with those who serve and share Him: He supplies the intelligence and facilities to come back to Him faster. — "Those to those who are constantly devoted to serving me with love, I give the…"

children.topic: We take one step, Krishna takes ten
children.note: As soon as Krishna sees interest in Him, He facilitates the journey with far more effort than we put in. — "Krishna wants us to go back to him more than we want to go it's…"

children.topic: Intelligence comes via Gita, devotees, guru
children.note: The understanding Krishna gives arrives through reading the Gita, associating with devotees, the spiritual master, and the competency He gives for service. — "Krishna sends us a spiritual master. Yes. Prasada Bhagavat Prasada. Through the mercy of the…"

children.topic: Prabhupada went to America with 40 rupees
children.note: With about 8 rand and a box of books, Prabhupada circled the globe 14 times in 11 years and opened over 108 temples. Unflinching faith in guru and Krishna brought everything. — "praar went with 8 rand to America he didn't know anybody he just had a…"

In the fourth verse Krishna destroys the darkness of ignorance with the lamp of knowledge; the devotee does not have to do this alone. — "Lord Krishna cleans our heart. We don't need to do that on our own. See…"

Other spiritual paths like vipassana meditation put the whole burden on the practitioner's own effort. — "they go and they seclude themselves, isolate themselves far from civilization, no talking, no social…"

children.topic: Bhakti needs only the desire to serve
children.note: Devotional service is easier than other paths because the devotee supplies the wish to please Krishna and Krishna handles the rest. — "The only thing that is required from the practitioner or from the devotey is the…"

children.topic: Prabhupada asks a sad devotee: are you chanting?
children.note: Bhakti is a happy process: contact with Krishna's names, prasadam or kirtan brings happiness, unlike traditions of self-torture. — "Are you chanting your rounds? Are you chanting Krishna's names? Because one who is doing…"

The essence seen in chapters 7 and 9 returns at the end of chapter 11, now broken into five things: work for me, be my devotee, make me supreme, avoid what pulls away, envy no one. — "My dear Arjun who engages in my pure devotional service free from the contamination of…"

children.topic: Work for me means work to please me
children.note: Mat-karma: doing everything for Krishna, with the small but decisive addition that it must actually please Him. — "Whatever we do, the result is to please Krishna. So someone cannot say, "Oh, I'm starting a liquor factory and I'll please Krishna." No, that will not please Krishna."
Mat-parama means nothing is superior to Krishna; the audience's laughter shows how hard that is in practice. — "If today you were asked that you can win 5 million rand or you can…"
The fifth item: no envy toward anyone. Together the five things are devotional service. — "nirvara means don't be envious to any living being no enemy nirv who is friendly…"

children.topic: Give Krishna your mind and intelligence
children.note: The highest level of the ladder in chapter 12: the earlier six chapters discussed the mind; now Krishna says what to do with it. — "Just fix your mind appropriately in the Supreme Personality of Godhead and engage all your…"

Corporates run mindfulness exercises because so much activity is mindless; Krishna asks for the mind first, then the intelligence too. — "Sometimes people do mindless activities, right? you know mindless the mind is not there. Therefore…"

children.topic: Result: you will live in me
children.note: Giving mind and intelligence to Krishna means living in Him without doubt. — "if you give me these two things what will happen what is the result you…"

children.topic: Can't fix the mind? Follow regulative principles
children.note: Abhyasa-yoga: since the mind is hard to control, Krishna offers the practice of regulation and detachment as the next option. — "Well, if you cannot fix your mind upon me without deviation, then follow the regulation…"

children.topic: The mind is like a rabbit
children.note: A running rabbit cannot be handed over; the mind must first be caught by regulation and detachment before it can be given to Krishna. — "So if you can't control the mind, how are you supposed to give the mind?…"

children.topic: Wake early, bathe, chant, offer, then work
children.note: Prabhupada's purport describes the principles of regulated freedom; most people, the lecturer jokes, fail at 'wake up early'. — "you wake up early in the morning you take a bath you chant some prayers…"

children.topic: Can't do that? Work for Krishna
children.note: The third rung: keep your ordinary work but give its result to Krishna. This is karma-yoga, distinct from direct bhakti like chanting or sweeping the temple. — "So Krishna is saying okay you can't give your mind you can't follow the practice…"

children.topic: Keep the activity, give the result
children.note: Donating part or all of one's earnings to the temple's feeding, book or prasad programmes is working for Krishna. — "you do your work you do your activity you don't change the activity but the…"
Giving all results is desireless (nishkama) karma; keeping some for oneself is sakama. — "if you give all of it then it is nishkam karma you you don't want…"

children.topic: The Uber driver who sponsors flowers
children.note: Example of working for Krishna: earn all day, deduct expenses, then sponsor flowers, prasad or a dress for the Deity from what is saved. — "I drive my Uber the whole day and then at the end of the day…"

Becoming a devotee means practising bhakti yoga, whose nine items include hearing, chanting, remembering, worshipping, offering prayers and obeisances. — "Hearing, chanting, remembering, worshiing him. That's coming next."

children.topic: Krishna sees the love, not the offering
children.note: Fruits, flowers and lamps matter only as carriers of love. — "Krishna doesn't look at the offering. He sees the love that you're giving him right…"

children.topic: Man walks in with nose in the sky
children.note: Obeisances sound simple but pride stops many; in some places even removing shoes and bowing is resisted. — "I saw some person coming in and their nose was pointing the sky. He walked…"

children.topic: Abandon all religion and surrender to Me
children.note: The second essence verse: give up bodily-level dharma and surrender; Krishna will deliver you from all sins, so do not fear. — "Abandon all varieties of religion. Which religion? The religion dealing with the body."

children.topic: No sin too great for Krishna
children.note: To those who feel too sinful for the temple: the temple is for decontamination, and past sins are no barrier to devotional service. — "there is no sin as great that Krishna cannot deal with"

children.topic: Gita's journey: soul, karma, jnana, modes, surrender
children.note: A recap of the whole Gita's flow, ending with Krishna saying forget all of that and just surrender. — "first he said you are the soul then he told us about karma how the…"

children.topic: The problem: we don't want to surrender
children.note: Life teaches never give up, so surrender feels counterintuitive; but the devotee knows that surrender is the way to win. — "The problem is we don't want to surrender. Right? Why should we surrender?"

The Gita's purpose is to bring the eternal soul to the eternal Lord in His eternal home; that process is surrender. — "So this is sanatan dharma. This is the definition Lord Krishna is giving surrender. We…"

Dragged into the assembly by Duhsasana, Draupadi could not save herself by strength; she was protected the moment she fully surrendered. — "Dropadi when the gambling match was going on she was put as a wager in…"

children.topic: One hand on the sari: nothing happened
children.note: While she still held on with one hand and called Govinda with the other, no help came. — "one hand go vinda please save me nothing happened."

children.topic: Both hands raised: Krishna came instantly
children.note: Before she finished the name Krishna was there, and Duhsasana pulled cloth enough to clothe all of Durban until he collapsed. — "so she raised both her hands and she chanted goinda it's up to you now…"

children.topic: Small fish swims upstream, hippo cannot
children.note: Taking shelter of the water, a little fish moves against the current; the fighting hippo cannot. As long as we fight instead of surrendering, we will not win. — "The hippo cannot swim upstream only has to go downstream cuz he's fighting he's fighting…"

children.topic: Bhakti is causeless: mercy, not karma
children.note: Answer to whether devotees must have had Krishna consciousness in a previous life: an unfinished yogi gets another chance, but devotional service begins by the mercy of devotees, not by past exposure. — "No, devotional service has no cause. It's causeless."

Far from India we should have had no information about Krishna; that we do is mercy, not karma. Our karma only brought us to this world. — "because Shilapraad came and he brought Krishna here to this continent Right? So that's the…"

children.topic: Prasad to pets: a double dose of mercy
children.note: Feeding prasad to anyone, pet or person, gives Krishna's mercy and the devotee's mercy; this is why devotees preach, distribute books and give out prasad. — "Prasada means Krishna's mercy. Prasad Krishna's mercy. And if I'm giving prashadada to someone not…"

Krishna had Arjuna declare that His devotee never perishes, because He never lets a devotee's promise fail; so devotees should be careful what they promise. — "the Lord can even break his promise but he doesn't break the promise of his…"

children.topic: Exercise: touch your nose, ear... yourself
children.note: A simple game: people can touch nose, ear and chin, but when told 'touch yourself' they do not know where to point. — "So I'm going to ask you to touch a part of your bodies right and…"

children.topic: Audit your day: body time vs soul time
children.note: A written exercise: note how much of the day goes to the body and how much to who you really are. — "So I'd like us to make a small note in our digital devices or notebooks.…"

children.topic: Exercise: offer one activity's result to Krishna
children.note: Pick an activity you are attached to (not your main one) and think how its result could be offered to Krishna. Chanting does not count - it is already a sacrifice. — "one activity that we do that we can offer the result to Krishna."

children.topic: Raising a devotee child: I did my part
children.note: A parent's example: expose the child to devotional service, but leave whether he becomes a devotee up to Krishna. — "Krishna I've done my part the rest is up to you whether he does become…"

children.topic: Finance student: use skills to serve temple
children.note: Beyond exam results, a career itself can be offered - advising devotees without charging, so money works for them. — "I can use the knowledge that I got in my financial studies to help the…"
A short silence to notice thousands of thoughts about past and future racing through the mind. — "So I'm going to stop speaking for a few seconds. Just observe internally what is…"
A study on screens found human attention now shorter than a goldfish's nine seconds. — "has an attention span of less than 9 seconds. You know goldfish."

children.topic: Influencers hook you in three seconds
children.note: Content creators exploit the short attention span; this is the distracted state we are in. — "in the very first 2 three seconds they put something so much attractive active or…"

children.topic: Find your awe in texts 19 to 40
children.note: Exercise: think of something in nature that inspires awe and find it in Krishna's list of opulences in chapter 10, texts 19 to 40. — "I would like you to think of one thing you find very beautiful in this…"

children.topic: Of trees I am the banyan
children.note: The banyan is auspicious, huge and generates oxygen around the clock; Krishna says of all trees He is the banyan. — "it's a 24-hour oxygen generating tree. Yes. And the size massive right it's not just…"

The ocean's length, breadth and depth are unknown; a whole plane vanishes in it. Krishna says of bodies of water He is the ocean. — "If you know, then look for MH370, right? One plane, you can't find it in…"

Among mountains the Himalayas, in the night sky the moon, by day the sun, among animals the lion: seeing their splendour should remind us of Krishna. — "If you want to look at what is brightest in the sky at night the…"

children.topic: Awe should trigger remembrance of Krishna
children.note: Krishna is the source of all beauty and splendour, so anything awe-inspiring is a spark of Him and a cue to remember Him. — "wherever we are inspired or there's a sense of awe or we are very happy…"

Audience exercise: goodness is clean, airy, spacious and full of light; passion is flashy and cluttered; ignorance is dirty, dark and smelly. — "what would a living quarter in the mode of goodness look like? Neat and organized.…"

children.topic: Passion: neon lights, glitter, teddy bears everywhere
children.note: A cousin's room with a thousand and one teddy bears and walls plastered with photos: you can tell a person's mode by entering their home. — "Flashy neon lights, artificial lighting, glitter everywhere, right? Lots of stuff everywhere."

children.topic: Judge your own lifestyle, not others
children.note: The knowledge of the modes is for self-assessment, after which Krishna prescribes devotional service to rise out of them. — "Lord Krishna is not doing that to make us judge others. Right? But it is…"

Pair exercise on eight everyday behaviours: calm study and selfless help are goodness, anxious working and competing are passion, postponing, late-night scrolling and over-sleeping are ignorance. — "studying calmly with a desire to understand. Goodness. Okay, I'm not hearing any other answer.…"

children.topic: Every place has its mode: temple, plaza, fish market
children.note: Walk from the temple half a kilometre to the plaza and the vibe changes; places too are governed by the modes. — "Ever been to a fish market? It's just opposite. Yeah. [laughter] or to the plaza…"

children.topic: Avoid lower modes by regulating lifestyle
children.note: Chanting and devotee association are the answers given, but they must be backed by a regulated life; Krishna is teaching lifestyle, not mumbo jumbo. — "We should try to be regulated in our practices. Yes. Regulated in our practices and…"

children.topic: Goodness: fixed times to wake, sleep, eat
children.note: People in goodness live regulated lives because they know what is right; passion does not know and ignorance does not care. — "Fixed times of waking, fixed times of sleeping, regulation in eating, regulation in work."

children.topic: Food in lower modes increases them
children.note: Recalling the earlier talk on foods by mode: what we eat and how we live feeds whichever mode it belongs to. — "So if we eat foods in the mode of passion and ignorance, our passion and…"

children.topic: This was a taster; the Gita is endless
children.note: Like a free sample at the mall, the week was only a taste; since the Gita is Krishna Himself, every reading gives more. — "Gita is endless. It it's it's doesn't have a beginning and doesn't have an end.…"

children.topic: Take the Gita out of the cellophane
children.note: Everyone should own a copy and read it daily rather than leave it wrapped at home. — "It's in the cellophane paper. No, you should open it and read it."

children.topic: Hack to living the Gita: chant
children.note: Becoming Krishna's devotee starts with chanting Hare Krishna; add Krishna to everything and remember Him through the day. — "The hack to living the Gita. It starts with our mouth. And it means we…"

maps.title: SB classes 2026 · Class 01 · Safety Under Krishna's Arms

nodeData.note: SB 1.14.35–36 · a class by HG Sri Gauranga Das. Continuing Yudhishthira's questions to the returning Arjuna, Prabhu explains why the Yadus live like the residents of Vaikuntha: Krishna and Balarama are with them. He traces the Lord's expansions from Balarama to the three Vishnus, then shows that this world is built to be unsafe, so real shelter, comfort and fearlessness are found only with Krishna. Questions cover the Brahman effulgence, the Lord's physical presence and the role of Jaya and Vijaya. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Prabhu recalls the setting: Yudhishthira is questioning Arjuna about his trip to Dwarka.

🎙 Prabhu at 04:57 (auto-transcript): “We are hearing Yudhishthir Maharaj asking Arjuna about his trip to Dwarka. Arjuna had gone to Dwarka but failed to return within seven months. Yudhishthira Maharaj observed inauspicious omens within the environment, within society and surmised that most probably Lord Krishna…”

Arjuna stayed away seven months; seeing ill omens in nature and society, Yudhishthira guessed Krishna had left the world, and Arjuna came back looking unhappy. Still Yudhishthira first asks about all their relatives in Mathura and Dwarka.

🎙 Prabhu at 05:08 (auto-transcript): “Arjuna had gone to Dwarka but failed to return within seven months. Yudhishthira Maharaj observed inauspicious omens within the environment, within society and surmised that most probably Lord Krishna is no longer on this planet. From his observation, he understood this and…”
Yudhishthira describes the Yadus as happy as Vaikuntha's residents, because Krishna and Balarama dwell among them and guard them.

Prabhu explains from the purport that creation is one quarter material and three quarters spiritual, and that for this world the Lord expands as the Purusha avatars.

🎙 Prabhu at 07:13 (auto-transcript): “Sushala Prabhupada is explaining in the purport that there is the material universe and then there is the spiritual universe. In the totality of creation, one quarter is the material universe and three quarters is the spiritual universe. Ekpad Vibhuti is known as the material…”

Balarama is Krishna's first expansion, the same Supreme Lord, differing only in function: He assists and serves Krishna in His pastimes. — “So Lord Balaram is the servant god”

🎙 Prabhu at 08:16 (auto-transcript): “So our scriptures, they tell us, Lord Balaram, he is the first expansion. And Lord Krishna has many, many types of expansions, many types of incarnations. And so for the purpose of creating this material world, the Lord expands himself into the Purusha avatars. Or the…”

From Balarama come Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha, with functions such as pervading everything, ego, intelligence and mind. From Sankarshana comes Narayana, and from Him a second set of four.

🎙 Prabhu at 09:41 (auto-transcript): “So from Lord Balaram There comes Chaturvyuha, an expansion of the Lord Which we read many times There are four of them Vasudev, Sankarshan, Pradyumna and Aniruddha and each of these four have their own specific functions. Vasudev means he is pervading the entire universe and…”

From the second Sankarshana comes Maha-Vishnu, then Garbhodakashayi and Kshirodakashayi Vishnu, each a Supersoul at a different level.

🎙 Prabhu at 10:54 (auto-transcript): “and from the second Sankarshan then comes Mahavishnu otherwise also known as Karunadakashai Vishnu or the super soul of the entire material existence and it is from this Mahavishnu who is lying in the causal ocean as Lord Srila Prabhupada is mentioning here that in the causal…”

Lying in the causal ocean, Maha-Vishnu exhales universes from His pores as empty shells and draws them back in as He inhales, again and again.

🎙 Prabhu at 11:15 (auto-transcript): “Mahavishnu who is lying in the causal ocean as Lord Srila Prabhupada is mentioning here that in the causal ocean there are so many bubbles and these bubbles are different different universes. He is saying these universes they are floating on the ocean like bubbles. So it is…”

children.topic: Ananta holds universes like mustard seeds
children.note:
Garbhodakashayi Vishnu enters each shell, creates the Garbhodaka ocean from His perspiration, and lies on Ananta, the many-hooded serpent who holds all universes like mustard seeds. From His navel a lotus grows, and on it Brahma is born.

🎙 Prabhu at 12:29 (auto-transcript): “So when he expands in each of these empty shells of the universe Garbodakashaya Vishnu enters all of them in his individual capacity. In each shell, Garbhodakashai Vishnu is there. So Garbhodakashai Vishnu is the super soul of the universe. Maha Vishnu, macro level of the…”

Kshirodakashayi Vishnu lives on the ocean of milk above even Brahmaloka. When troubled, the demigods stand on its shore with Brahma; they cannot see the Lord, and only Brahma hears His instructions.

🎙 Prabhu at 14:43 (auto-transcript): “and then Garbhodakashai Vishnu expounds one final time as Shirodakashai Vishnu. Shirodakashai Vishnu within this universe. So we are looking at from Mahavishnu an empty shell comes out, then from that in that shell Garbhodakashai Vishnu enters and then when he enters the…”

Prabhu sums up: Maha-Vishnu is the Supersoul of all material existence, Garbhodakashayi of each universe, and Kshirodakashayi of every heart and atom — the same Supersoul Parikshit saw.

🎙 Prabhu at 17:14 (auto-transcript): “So Maha Vishnu super soul of material existence. Garbhutha Kashaya Vishnu super soul of the universe and Shirodha Kashaya Vishnu super soul in the heart. Present in each and every atom. So although we are looking at three expansions and we are looking at Krishna and his…”

All these expansions are one person. We are used to one soul in one body, so the spiritual reality of many forms and one soul is beyond our experience and causes confusion. — “spiritual world is many bodies one soul”

🎙 Prabhu at 17:29 (auto-transcript): “So although we are looking at three expansions and we are looking at Krishna and his expansion as Lord Balaram and then the Chaturvyoham but one thing we need to understand is is the same person. This is where so much confusion comes in because here in this world we are…”

Yudhishthira compares Dwarka to the ocean of milk, a Vaikuntha atmosphere within the material universe.

🎙 Prabhu at 18:58 (auto-transcript): “So therefore Maharaj Yudhishthir here is remembering the Shira Sagar and comparing the residence of Dwarka to this place, the ocean of milk. When the ocean of milk is the abode of the Lord, There is a Vaikuntha planet or a Vaikuntha atmosphere within this material universe.…”

Dhruvaloka is another spiritual planet here. As embassies in Nairobi follow their own country's rules, such places do not run under material laws.

🎙 Prabhu at 19:27 (auto-transcript): “There is another planet like this in our universe. That planet is known as Dhruvaloka. It is one of the Vaikuntha planets but it is here in the material world. Just like you have an embassy. So in Nairobi we have so many embassies. but the rules of chenya are not applicable…”

Dwarka was Vaikuntha on earth because Krishna and Balarama were there; Vrindavan, where He played, still does not function like the rest of the world.

🎙 Prabhu at 20:44 (auto-transcript): “Why? Because Lord Krishna was there and Lord Ananta were there. Wherever Lord Krishna is present, then that place is not different from the spiritual world. We look at Vrindavan, where Lord Krishna performed his pastimes. Even today, thousands of devotees go there because…”

Vaikuntha means free from fear; this world is always fearful. Even the comfortable worry how long their comfort will last, and our defending comes from fear. — “We are always fearful in this world.”

🎙 Prabhu at 21:26 (auto-transcript): “What is Vaikuntha? Vaikuntha means, Shra Prabhupada is mentioning here, a place that is free from fear. Kuntha is known as the material world. There is always fear. And this is always existing. Fear is always there. Our conditional life is characterized by eating, sleeping,…”

Many moved to Dubai for safety and prosperity, but when war broke out and it was attacked, thousands left in fear.

🎙 Prabhu at 22:23 (auto-transcript): “Many people would go to Dubai and they would think Dubai is safe, it's prosperous. Here Yudhishthira Maharaj is speaking about Dwaraka, how prosperous it is how safe it is and people would think oh Dubai is so safe so prosperous quality of life is so nice and so many people…”

Expecting not to be pricked in a forest of thorns is unintelligent; this world is designed to be unsafe. — “It's a forest of thorns.”

🎙 Prabhu at 23:27 (auto-transcript): “find a safe place because the world itself is designed to be unsafe you go into a forest of thorns and if you expect that oh i will not be pricked then that is not very intelligent It's a forest of thorns. You will be pricked somewhere. So this world is designed, this…”

Indraprastha was so opulent that Duryodhana was allured, yet Yudhishthira says only the Yadus are truly safe, because the Lord's arms protect them. Even a city far ahead in technology is not safe.

🎙 Prabhu at 24:34 (auto-transcript): “Otherwise even Indraprastha was a very opulent city. Very prosperous. Duryodhana also got allured by the prosperity of Indraprastha. But Yudhishthira Maharaj is saying no we may be materially prosperous but we are not safe. Who are safe? Yadavas are safe. They are materially…”

We crave permanence because it means safety. On Kipande Road at midnight people run, not walk; yet in this world we think we are safe in bodies that age, sicken and die.

🎙 Prabhu at 26:31 (auto-transcript): “Just walk on our Kipande road down here at midnight. Most people will not walk, they will run. We see it always, people running up and down because they know if we delay here, we will get robbed. So whenever we go to an unsafe place, we don't want to spend a second necessary…”

Prabhu cites Sukadeva Goswami: the deluded man trusts his soldiers — body, wife, children and clan — though he sees them all falling around him.

🎙 Prabhu at 27:24 (auto-transcript): “we think oh I am safely protected by my body Sukhdev Goswami mentions this The gross material is Even though he is seeing He does not see He thinks oh I will be protected By my soldiers Who are these soldiers Deha My body My body is protecting me Apatya and Kalatra, my sons…”

Where are our grandfathers and great-grandfathers? Relatives die all around, yet we think we are safe. Safety is not in wealth or a big clan but with Krishna and Balarama.

🎙 Prabhu at 28:34 (auto-transcript): “They are all falling. Where is our grandfather? Some people may have their grandfathers. Then where is our great grandfather? No longer. relatives dying left right center all around us but under the illusion we think we are safe Yudhishthira Maharaj here is saying safety is…”

The brothers come for the world's auspiciousness; Prabhu recalls Kaviraj Goswami calling them a rising sun and moon that dispel ignorance. — “auspiciousness can only be found”

🎙 Prabhu at 29:21 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj is saying both of them they're here for Mangalaya they're the ones who are bringing all auspiciousness. Kaviraj Goswami also he mentions in the beginning of Chaitanya Charita Amrita that these two brothers have come to dissipate. They are like the rising sun of…”

Prahlada says people take shelter of what is unworthy of shelter. Offered a ladder with missing rungs, you would refuse it; not knowing their interest lies in Vishnu, people climb such ladders. — “You'd say, no, I don't trust this ladder.”

🎙 Prabhu at 30:16 (auto-transcript): “Prahlad Maharaj knew this. He is saying Durasraya Durasraya means something that is not worthy of taking shelter. Just like if I was to give you a ladder to climb and that ladder was a rickety ladder right? that had a few rungs missing and didn't look like it could carry your…”

Those who struggle hope one day to tell interviewers how they got out of it. Our inherent nature seeks safety and comfort, and with them comes happiness.

🎙 Prabhu at 31:18 (auto-transcript): “everyone is looking for safety everyone is looking for comfort no one wants struggle those who are struggling they are going on with the hope that oh one day this struggle will stop one day I will make it one day the days of my struggle will be left behind and I can write in…”

When Kalayavana and Jarasandha attacked Mathura, Krishna built Dwarka in the ocean and moved everyone there overnight, staying behind with Balarama to fight. Dwarka could only be reached by flying in on 'Garuda Airways'. — “And so the Yadavas knew safety equals being with Krishna.”

🎙 Prabhu at 32:31 (auto-transcript): “The same families were there in Mathura and Lord Krishna, after killing Kamsa, he attracted attention of Kalayavana and Jarasandha. So Kalayavana came with his massive army to attack Mathura. That was the plan along with Jarasandha. and so Lord Krishna said okay Mathura…”

As Kunti prayed earlier, the Pandavas knew their prosperity and safety came from Krishna and begged Him not to go back to Dwarka.

🎙 Prabhu at 35:05 (auto-transcript): “We read earlier in the 8th chapter Kunti Maharani's prayers and where she is saying now that we are safe you are leaving us then we will not be safe anymore. You cannot leave us. Now that we seem that we are prosperous but actually this prosperity is because of you. Kunti…”

children.topic: Why fear when God is there?
children.note:
Like the bumper sticker, the Yadus lived without fear and no one could defeat them, because Krishna was with them. — “Why fear when God is there?”

🎙 Prabhu at 37:13 (auto-transcript): “Some people put a bumper sticker on the car. Why fear when God is there? So the Yadavas were living by this. There was no fear because Krishna was there. They knew nothing can happen to us. And indeed the Yadavas were invincible. Nobody could defeat them. Nobody could…”

What the world searches for and fails to find, Yudhishthira gives the clue to: to be safe and happy we must take shelter of Krishna and live with Him.

🎙 Prabhu at 38:12 (auto-transcript): “For us, it means if we want to be safe, if we want to be comfortable, if we want to enjoy, then we also have to connect ourselves to Lord Krishna. We also have to take shelter of Lord Krishna. We also have to live with Lord Krishna. What everyone else is looking for and being…”

Questions and comments at the end of class.

🎙 Prabhu at 38:56 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, if there are any questions or comments. Yes. So the question is, what is Brahman infurgence? Brahman infurgence is light. What it looks like, it looks like light. It is light. You know, but this light is not glaring light.”

children.topic: Q1 · What is the Brahman effulgence?
children.note:
A devotee asks what the Brahman effulgence is.

🎙 Prabhu at 39:20 (auto-transcript): “So the question is, what is Brahman infurgence? Brahman infurgence is light. What it looks like, it looks like light. It is light. You know, but this light is not glaring light. It's not like, oh, you can't look at it. No, it's very soothing, but it's bright everywhere. It's…”

It is light, not glaring but soothing, like Nairobi's clear sky lit everywhere; it comes from Krishna's body. Brahman, the Lord's impersonal feature, is not the same as Brahma.

🎙 Prabhu at 39:28 (auto-transcript): “Brahman infurgence is light. What it looks like, it looks like light. It is light. You know, but this light is not glaring light. It's not like, oh, you can't look at it. No, it's very soothing, but it's bright everywhere. It's like the sky. Right now we have a clear sky here…”

children.topic: A green parrot in a green tree
children.note:
Souls in the Brahman do not lose identity. Like a green parrot in a green tree, they are hard to see from afar but still there, floating in that sky. — “The Vedas, they explain just like a green parrot sitting in a green tree.”

🎙 Prabhu at 41:25 (auto-transcript): “So in that light, the souls, and that's what Krishna explains in the Gita, that even if we go into Brahman, we don't become identity-less. We don't lose our identity. The Vedas, they explain just like a green parrot sitting in a green tree. So, if you try to look for the…”

children.topic: Q2 · Is His physical presence needed?
children.note:
Is one safe only when the Lord is physically present?

🎙 Prabhu at 42:50 (auto-transcript): “So does the physical presence of the Lord only give safety? And if someone is not physically present with the Lord, are they safe? So here, in terms of the narrative, the Pandavas of course were always connected with the Lord. they have taken shelter, they were eternally…”

The Pandavas were always connected with Krishna, but His physical absence is painful. The Pandavas praised the Yadus for having a city built by Him, and the Yadus praised the Pandavas because Krishna sat in their assembly.

🎙 Prabhu at 43:19 (auto-transcript): “So here, in terms of the narrative, the Pandavas of course were always connected with the Lord. they have taken shelter, they were eternally associated with the Lord. But in terms of the narrative, because Yudhishthir Maharaj is already having that conception in his head that…”

Why did the Vaikuntha gatekeepers, born as demons, worship demigods rather than the Lord?

🎙 Prabhu at 45:43 (auto-transcript): “So why did the gatekeepers of Vaikuntha, Jay and Vijay, when they came here as demons, why didn't they worship Lord Krishna, why did they worship the demigods? Why did they worship Lord Krishna indirectly by worshiping the demigods?”

They came to be the Lord's enemies, and one does not approach one's enemy, so Hiranyakashipu went to Brahma for power. Such things — like the meeting of Rama and Parashurama — are all part of the Lord's pastimes, understood through the acharyas.

🎙 Prabhu at 46:29 (auto-transcript): “Because they were fulfilling a particular character, a particular role. They were enemies of Lord Krishna. Why would you go to your enemy? Hiranyakashipu decided, oh Brahma is the greatest living being in this universe, so I will approach him. he had enmity with Vishnu he is…”
